book.title: The Penguin Book of Financial Times Crosswords, volume 1

clue.text: State papers can be very revealing

parts.note: to state something is to say or speak it
papers bound together make up volumes, in a loose sense

explanation.surface: Government documents, once released, may expose a great deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State papers' reads as one official phrase, but 'State' is a verb here. The link between papers and volumes is a loose one.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something that tells a great deal without words, so it means being highly telling or informative.

clue.text: Editor of journal is decorated

parts.note: a newspaper is a journal
the usual abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: Someone running a magazine has been given an honour.
explanation.walkthrough: The editor 'of' the journal comes after it in the answer: the journal's letters come first.
explanation.definitionFit: Walls that have been hung with wallpaper have been decorated, so the past participle fits.

clue.text: Nobody is missing full board and lodging

definitions.meaning: first meaning: everyone has been located, every person accounted for
second meaning: an old phrase in job advertisements for wages that include food and housing

explanation.walkthrough: In old British job advertisements a servant's wage 'and all found' meant meals and a room were provided on top of pay.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally says every person has been located, and idiomatically means meals and accommodation are supplied with employment.

clue.text: What one thinks of a post-card

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a picture postcard showing a scene, traditionally sold as one of these

explanation.surface: Someone is asked their opinion of a card that arrived in the mail.
explanation.walkthrough: Seaside shops sold picture postcards of the scenery under this name.
explanation.definitionFit: An opinion is a personal outlook, and a picture postcard shows a scenic outlook from some resort or landmark.

clue.text: Dissolute client upset by debts

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and thrown into disorder, so the letters before it are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, then jumbled
an IOU is a written acknowledgement of a debt

explanation.surface: A wayward customer is distressed by what they owe.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone living without moral restraint, especially in pleasure-seeking or sexual behaviour.

clue.text: Ministry of Transport has to make up a slogan

parts.note: the initials of the former British government department, also known from the annual vehicle test
taken as written

explanation.surface: A government department is told it must come up with a catchphrase.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOT is the British roadworthiness test, named after the Ministry of Transport.
explanation.definitionFit: A short phrase summing up a principle or cause works as both a campaign catchphrase and a guiding maxim.

clue.text: Curse company taken in by swell

indicators.note: something taken in by another is held within it, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a swell of the sea is a surge
the usual abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A firm is swamped and overwhelmed by a rising wave.
explanation.definitionFit: A plague or affliction that torments people is a curse upon them, the noun sense of each word.

clue.text: Could station get over such decoration?

parts.note: a major London railway terminus
to get over a road or river is to cross it

explanation.surface: A question whether a railway station could earn a medal for bravery.
explanation.walkthrough: Victoria is one of London's main railway stations. The answer is Britain's highest award for gallantry.
explanation.definitionFit: The medal is the top British military honour, and medals worn on a uniform are called decorations.

clue.text: Screen appearance obtained for Italian by a ruse

parts.note: a person from Venice is an Italian
a blind is a pretext or decoy meant to deceive

explanation.surface: An actor from Italy wins a film role through trickery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screen appearance' looks like a film role, but 'Screen' alone is the definition. A blind is also something kept up for appearance's sake, which may be why that word is there.
explanation.definitionFit: A window covering of adjustable horizontal slats shuts out light and view, so it is a kind of screen.

clue.text: One Frenchman on beat finds something stimulating

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
M is the abbreviation for monsieur
a pulse is a regular beat

explanation.surface: A French policeman walking his beat comes across something exciting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On beat' suggests a policeman on patrol; here 'on' just places one piece after the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden urge or a push that drives action is a spur or stimulus, something that prompts movement.

clue.text: Each dot could represent a pole

indicators.note: the letters could be rearranged to stand for something else, so they are reordered

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: On a map, every dot might mark a polar point or a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: The negative electrode of a cell or valve is one of its two poles, the electrical sense rather than a stick.

clue.text: Trunk goes to the right like this

parts.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right
'do it so' means do it like this

explanation.surface: A road direction: the main route turns right like so.
explanation.definitionFit: The human body without head or limbs is called the trunk, and the anatomical word names the same part.

clue.text: Going the right way during training

definitions.meaning: first meaning: heading along the intended route
second meaning: attending a series of lessons

explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads the phrase literally: someone on a training programme is on a course.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship or plan holding its planned heading is well placed, and a trainee attending classes is enrolled in instruction.

clue.text: A soft centre, dearest

parts.note: soft and gentle, as in sweet music
the heart of something is its centre

explanation.surface: A chocolate with a soft filling is someone's favourite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A soft centre' looks like a chocolate from a box; it splits into two words instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are affectionate forms of address for a loved one or romantic partner.

clue.text: Crop can be produced in Yorkshire area with drive

parts.note: Yorkshire was historically divided into three ridings
to whip horses or cattle is to drive them on

explanation.surface: A farm harvest can be grown in a Yorkshire district with enough effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crop' looks like a harvest; it is the short whip used by riders. The ridings were the old administrative divisions of the English county of Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: A riding crop is a short stick with a loop used by horse riders, the same item as the answer.

clue.text: Fairy is ripe for transforming …

indicators.note: the word is there to be transformed, changed into a new shape

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A fairy is ready to work some magical change.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots carry the sentence into the next clue, but each half is solved on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: In Persian myth a peri is a beautiful supernatural being, the word used in English for a kind of sprite.

clue.text: Unworthy shot made during game

parts.note: base means low or contemptible
shot fired from a cannon is ball, as in ball and powder

explanation.surface: A cheap shot was played in the middle of a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made during' only joins the pieces to the definition; it does not mean one goes inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: The American bat-and-ball sport is a specific example of a game.

clue.text: …shield for members

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the heraldic device painted on a shield, a coat of this
second meaning: limbs of the body

explanation.walkthrough: The dots continue the previous clue's sentence, but this clue stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Heraldic bearings displayed on a shield are a family's emblem, and the upper limbs are bodily members.

clue.text: Interferes with sounding of gongs

indicators.note: sounding means what is heard when the word is spoken, not its spelling

parts.note: gongs is British slang for military decorations

explanation.surface: Someone disturbs the ringing of a set of gongs.
explanation.walkthrough: Gong is British slang for a medal or award.
explanation.definitionFit: To poke into other people's affairs uninvited is to interfere, the verb in the same third-person form.

clue.text: Our patient gets muddled over name

indicators.note: muddled things are mixed up and confused, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A hospital patient becomes confused about what he is called.
explanation.definitionFit: A good name is a standing in public esteem, as in to make a name for yourself.

clue.text: Can't be bothered feeling troubles are in it

indicators.note: something troubled is stirred up and disturbed, so the following letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Apathy sets in when worries pile up.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethargy, the sluggish reluctance to act or make any effort, is the everyday sense of the physics term.

clue.text: Cardinal understanding danger sign

parts.note: cardinal red is the scarlet of a cardinal's robes
to see the light is to understand

explanation.surface: A senior cleric grasps the meaning of a warning signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A stop signal on a road or railway warns of hazard ahead, a classic warning indicator.

clue.text: Annoyed by one tax

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
rates were a British local property tax

explanation.surface: Someone is cross about a single levy.
explanation.walkthrough: Rates were the local property tax in Britain before the council tax.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone angry or irritated, the same adjective sense.

clue.text: One quarter fortunate being in Surrey

parts.note: east is one of the four quarters of the compass
loosely, as in 'it was as well' meaning it was fortunate

explanation.surface: A lucky inhabitant lives in one district of Surrey.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey is a county just south-west of London. The definition is a place 'being in Surrey', and the link between fortunate and well is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Ewell is a town in the English county of Surrey, near Epsom, so it is a place located there.

clue.text: It's a blended wine

indicators.note: a blended wine is mixed together, so these letters are mixed

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Something poured is described as a mixed vintage.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling white from Piedmont in northern Italy, an example of the drink.

clue.text: She's connected with royalty, old fruit

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the wife, mother or daughter of a Muslim ruler
second meaning: a dried grape, fruit that has been kept and shrivelled

explanation.walkthrough: 'Old fruit' is dated British slang for a friend, which is the misdirection; here it means a dried grape.
explanation.definitionFit: The title belongs to a sultan's wife or female relative, and the word also names a dried seedless grape.

clue.text: Old Bob catches small animal in spruce

parts.note: bob was slang for a shilling, abbreviated s in old British money
a marten is a small weasel-like mammal

explanation.surface: An elderly man named Bob traps a little creature among the conifers.
explanation.walkthrough: A bob was a shilling in pre-decimal British money. The two pieces simply sit side by side; 'catches' does not put one inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: To spruce up is to tidy or make neat, the same verb sense as making something look trim.

clue.text: Bloomer made by gentle conqueror

parts.note: sweet and gentle, as in a sweet temper
William the Conqueror invaded England in 1066

explanation.surface: A blunder committed by a mild-mannered invader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a mistake; it is something that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: The garden plant with dense clusters of fragrant flowers is something that blooms, a flowering plant.
